Member A
Member B

requirement.summary: [Tech] Impact of Changing RabbitMQ createQueue durable from false to true on TMS sendMessageToMQ - Dev
requirement.description:
Changing the durable parameter in createQueue from false to true does not directly alter WebSocket connection behavior or real-time transmission performance.

However, it changes the semantics of whether queues and messages survive broker restarts, which indirectly affects how WebSocket clients experience reconnections and service restarts.

Direct Impact: On the WebSocket Connection Itself

- WebSocket connection establishment, heartbeats, and reconnection logic: These are primarily determined by the client SDK, the server-side WebSocket handling (e.g., Spring WebSocket, STOMP over WebSocket), and the network layer, and are not directly related to whether the queue is durable.

- Real-time latency and throughput: According to RabbitMQ documentation, in most cases, whether a queue is durable does not significantly affect throughput or latency; differences are only noticeable in scenarios with extremely high-frequency queue creation/deletion.

In other words, simply changing an existing queue from non-durable to durable will not cause currently connected WebSocket clients to suddenly become slower or change their connection behavior.

Indirect Impact: Semantic Changes for WebSocket Use Cases

The key difference lies in whether messages persist after restarts and reconnections:

durable = false (Original Setting)

- The queue exists only in memory; after a broker restart, the queue is deleted and all messages inside it are lost.

- Implications for WebSocket clients:

-

- If the client briefly disconnects but the broker does not restart, messages may still remain in the queue (depending on whether you use temporary/auto-delete queues).

-

- Once the broker restarts (deployment, failure, upgrade), all messages buffered in that queue are lost; after reconnection, the client will only receive messages produced after the restart.

- This is more suitable for “real-time state” scenarios, such as:

-

- Real-time notifications, latest chat messages, live dashboard data, where only “current and future” data is needed and historical backfill is not required.

durable = true (New Setting)

- The queue definition is persisted to disk and automatically recreated after a broker restart; if messages are also sent as persistent (delivery mode 2), those messages will be restored after restart.

- Implications for WebSocket clients:

-

- After a broker restart, when a client re-subscribes to the same durable queue, it can continue to receive previously unconsumed persistent messages (provided the messages themselves are persistent and the client has a proper ack mechanism).

-

- If you combine this with STOMP durable subscriptions (e.g., setting durable: true in headers and using a fixed subscription id), clients can receive messages that accumulated while they were offline upon reconnection.

- Suitable for scenarios requiring “at-least-once delivery” or “offline backfill”, such as:

-

- Critical business notifications, order status changes, task result callbacks, which should not be lost due to a broker restart.

Practical Considerations

- Messages must also be persistent

Setting the queue to durable alone is not enough; if messages are still sent as transient (many clients default to transient), messages will still be lost on broker restart.

-

- You need to set deliveryMode = 2 (or the equivalent persistent option in your language) on the publisher side.

- Client ack mechanism must align

To guarantee no message loss, consumers (the backend services feeding WebSocket clients) should ack to RabbitMQ only after confirming the frontend has actually received the message; otherwise, messages may still be lost or duplicated if the service crashes.

- Avoid queue buildup causing WebSocket disconnections or delays

After switching to durable, if clients are offline for long periods or consume slowly, messages can accumulate, potentially leading to:

-

- A large burst of messages on reconnection, causing frontend lag or connection timeouts.

-

- If there is a reverse proxy (e.g., nginx) with proxy buffering enabled, you may see “delayed messages” or “disconnections”; proxy settings may need adjustment.

-

- In practice, temporary WebSocket users are often given auto-delete queues or queues with x-expires so the broker cleans them up automatically.

- Changes in RabbitMQ 4.x

Starting from RabbitMQ 4.0, support for non-exclusive, non-durable queues will be removed; the trend is to encourage the use of durable or quorum queues.

Practical Recommendations (for WebSocket Scenarios)

- For real-time, disposable messages (e.g., live chat, real-time stock ticks):

-

- You can continue using non-durable or temporary queues to reduce disk I/O and the risk of message buildup.

- For critical business messages that must not be lost on broker restart:

-

- Change the queue to durable, and at the same time:

-

-

- Publish messages as persistent (delivery mode 2).

-

-

- Use publisher confirms.

-

-

- Have consumers use manual ack, and only ack after confirming the frontend has received the message.

- If you are concerned about offline message accumulation:

-

- Use short-lived queues per WebSocket session (auto-delete or with x-expires), or periodically clean up old messages.

Changing the durable parameter in createQueue from false to true does not directly alter WebSocket connection behavior or real-time transmission performance.

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - Error occurs when clicking reservation in Operation after creating or editing reservation online
requirement.description:
Preconditions:

- The current outlet has a reservation, e.g. Confirmation No. E0007

Steps:

1. Login to TMS Operation > Elvar-Hong Kong (E0414) > Stay on the Current View page

2. Login to Online > Click "Retrieve Booking Record" button > Input Reservation info and click the "Search" button > Click "Edit" button

3. Change the number of people > Click the "Submit button"

4. Immediately go back to TMS Operation >  Click the reservation with Confirmation No. E0007

Actual Result:

- Error prompt is shown: "Something went wrong. Error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')"

- Reproduce video: 20260804_150135.mp4

Expect Result:

- Enter the Reservation Record page normally
requirement.release_notes:
Bug Fixing: [Jira-67826] TMS 2.0 - Error occurs when clicking reservation in Operation after creating or editing reservation online
Descriptions:
After creating online booking data and pushing it to Operations via WebSocket, clicking to view the booking details displays an error message on the page: "Something went wrong. Error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')".
Setup:
Prerequisite: WebSocket is enabled.
Operation enters the Current View, stays on the booking outlet and period selection screen, and then creates an online booking.
After the WebSocket pushes the booking record to Operation, click to view the booking details.
The page does not return an error and the booking details can be viewed normally.
Period configuration payment.
Create an online booking and complete the payment.
After the WebSocket pushes the data to Operation, click the booking to view its details, where the payment amount can be seen.
